candidate.answerReason: A self-reciprocal number multiplied by itself equals 1, so its absolute value must be 1; both signs work. Zero has no reciprocal, C omits -1, and the reciprocal of 1/2 refutes D.

methods.label: Check reciprocal facts and reject false claims
methods.explanation: Since \(1\times1=1\) and \((-1)\times(-1)=1\), the numbers whose reciprocals equal themselves are 1 and \(-1\). The number 0 has no reciprocal. The reciprocal of \(1/2\) is 2, which is greater than \(1/2\).
